NoDPI runs an HTTP(S) proxy server on your device. Traffic sent through it is unblocked: the ClientHello of blocked domains is fragmented around SNI and sent with disorder.

1. Start the proxy.
2. Open Wi-Fi settings, edit your network, set Proxy to Manual and enter the host and port shown above.
3. Alternatively, set the proxy only in an app or browser that supports HTTP proxies.

The proxy does not change your IP address and does not encrypt traffic.
One or several domains separated by spaces, commas or new lines. Subdomains are covered automatically
The list will be replaced with the default YouTube domains
These domains are already in the blacklist
The \"All domains\" mode is on: every domain is unblocked and the blacklist is not used
The \"Auto\" mode is on: domains that turn out to be blocked are added here automatically
Cloudflare: sent without fragmentation, it does not help there
Listen on 0.0.0.0 so other devices (for example, via hotspot) can use the proxy
Only domains from the blacklist are unblocked
Every domain is unblocked, the blacklist is ignored. Sites on Cloudflare are sent without fragmentation: it cannot unblock them and only breaks them
Blacklist plus automatic detection: a domain whose TLS handshake times out is added to the blacklist
The domain itself or any of its parent domains must be in the blacklist
Also matches any domain that contains a blacklist entry
Send the first fragment with TTL 1 so that DPI sees fragments out of order. Turn off if sites stop opening
Basic proxy authentication, useful with local network access
Start the proxy automatically after the device boots
Unrestricted: the system will not stop the proxy
Restricted: the system may stop the proxy in the background. Tap to allow
The proxy status is shown in the notification
Disabled: the proxy works, but its notification is hidden
Android version of NoDPI, a utility for bypassing DPI. The proxy fragments the TLS ClientHello of blocked domains around SNI and sends it with disorder, exactly like the desktop version.
To keep the proxy running when the app is closed, it is better to give it a little more freedom. You can change this later in Settings.
Otherwise the system may stop the proxy in the background

Remove the manual Wi-Fi proxy once. NoDPI connects and disconnects automatically. Uses the Android VPN slot; no external VPN server.
Select at least one installed app before starting VPN.
Open NoDPI and grant VPN permission.
The local VPN engine stopped. Connection released.
Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1) instead of physical-network DNS. Domain names are sent to Cloudflare, including for SOCKS5 apps. Manual proxy resolves IPv4; VPN forwards real DNS replies.
Local VPN requires Android 10 or newer. Manual proxy is available on this device.
Local bypass applies to all HTTPS domains of captured apps, with Cloudflare exclusions. External SOCKS5 apps use the external route. Domain lists apply only to manual proxy.

Selected apps use your external server; other captured apps use local bypass. No direct fallback. External UDP is blocked. DNS uses the resolver selected below. SOCKS5 does not itself encrypt traffic.
Choose at least one app. External-route apps are automatically captured by VPN.
Password is encrypted with Android Keystore. After restoring a backup you may need to enter it again.

Runs an explicit DNS → proxy TCP → destination CONNECT → certificate-verified TLS → HTTP response check. Start NoDPI first for local bypass. This tests the chosen route, not another app’s live connection.
Only the external SOCKS5 apps are selected.
A route shows where traffic is directed, not whether a site is reachable. Use connection diagnostics for a network check.

Export app routes, SOCKS5 address, bypass options and domain list. Passwords and usernames are excluded. Local proxy binding/authentication, autostart and consent are not transferred. Import does not reconnect a running VPN.
Settings imported. Re-enter SOCKS5 credentials if required, then apply and reconnect.

The file contains %1$d app selections and %2$d domains. The domain list will be replaced. SOCKS5 requiring authentication stays blocked until credentials are entered again. Current connections keep their applied settings until reconnection.
Re-enter SOCKS5 username and password after import before applying these routes.

Use IPv4 for captured apps. VPN DNS suppresses AAAA and HTTPS/SVCB answers; cached IPv6 connections are rejected without bypassing VPN. Apps with their own DNS may need restarting. IPv6-only services will be unavailable. Apply and reconnect after changing.
